edits.value_json: Shang oracle-bone forms are described as mountain outlines. Shang and Western Zhou bronze forms vary, showing three or five peaks, either filled or outlined; later forms are described as stylized. The listed script stages do not establish a continuous sequence of graphic changes. The selected small-seal-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient specimen.

The landscape-noun sense is supported in early inscriptional and literary contexts and remains an ordinary current meaning. 《字源》 describes the basic sense as a high, pointed part of the ground. Its earliest attestation and deeper chronology are unresolved.
